response.sql: WITH spatial_with_project AS (SELECT sp.arcref, p.fundflux, CASE WHEN sp.boxx IS NOT NULL AND sp.boxz IS NOT NULL AND sp.boxz != 0 THEN sp.boxx / sp.boxz ELSE NULL END AS ratio FROM scanspatial sp INNER JOIN projects p ON sp.arcref = p.arcregistry), project_ratios AS (SELECT arcref, fundflux, AVG(ratio) AS project_ratio FROM spatial_with_project WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL GROUP BY arcref, fundflux), source_averages AS (SELECT fundflux, AVG(project_ratio) AS source_avg_ratio FROM project_ratios GROUP BY fundflux), margins AS (SELECT pr.arcref, pr.fundflux, pr.project_ratio AS ratio, pr.project_ratio - sa.source_avg_ratio AS margin FROM project_ratios pr JOIN source_averages sa ON pr.fundflux = sa.fundflux) SELECT arcref, fundflux, ratio, margin FROM margins ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: When a project has multiple scanspatial records, the project's single ratio for comparison is the average of all valid (non-NULL) boxx÷boxz ratios across its records. This aggregates multiple spatial records per project into one comparative value.

The phrase 'simple average ratio of the projects in their own funding source' means: for each funding source, average the aggregated project-level ratios (not the raw average of all spatial records). This treats each project as a unit within its source group.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each scanspatial record individually: calculate boxx÷boxz for each record, average these ratios per funding source across all records (without project-level aggregation), then rank individual records by how much their ratio beats the source average. This would return up to 10 spatial records, potentially multiple per project.
